title: DASS-21: Depression, Anxiety and Stress
summary: A well known 21-question check on low mood, anxiety and stress over the past week, scored the official way.
clinicianNotes: Published instrument (DASS-21), wording as published; the scoring sheet states it is free to use. Each subscale has 7 items; sums are doubled and compared with the published cut-offs (Normal, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Extremely severe). It is dimensional and has no diagnostic implications. It should not replace a face to face clinical interview. Item 21 (life was meaningless) is listed under 'Items to look at together' when answered 3; this is a choice for the reviewing psychologist and can be changed in the pack file. Set for Adults only; whether to offer it to Teens is for the psychologist to decide. No local norms are available.
prompt: Please read each statement and choose how much it applied to you. There are no right or wrong answers. Do not spend too much time on any statement.

scale.label: Did not apply to me at all
Applied to me to some degree, or some of the time
Applied to me to a considerable degree or a good part of the time
Applied to me very much or most of the time

source.attribution: DASS-21, Lovibond, S. H. & Lovibond, P. F. (1995). Manual for the Depression Anxiety & Stress Scales (2nd ed.). Sydney: Psychology Foundation.

subscales.label: Depression
subscales.description: Low mood, hopelessness, loss of interest and energy.

subscales.label: Anxiety
subscales.description: Physical arousal, panic and fearful feelings.

subscales.label: Stress
subscales.description: Difficulty relaxing, nervous tension and irritability.

items.text: I found it hard to wind down
I was aware of dryness of my mouth
I couldn't seem to experience any positive feeling at all
I experienced breathing difficulty (e.g. excessively rapid breathing, breathlessness in the absence of physical exertion)
I found it difficult to work up the initiative to do things
I tended to over-react to situations
I experienced trembling (e.g. in the hands)
I felt that I was using a lot of nervous energy
I was worried about situations in which I might panic and make a fool of myself
I felt that I had nothing to look forward to
I found myself getting agitated
I found it difficult to relax
I felt down-hearted and blue
I was intolerant of anything that kept me from getting on with what I was doing
I felt I was close to panic
I was unable to become enthusiastic about anything
I felt I wasn't worth much as a person
I felt that I was rather touchy
I was aware of the action of my heart in the absence of physical exertion (e.g. sense of heart rate increase, heart missing a beat)
I felt scared without any good reason
I felt that life was meaningless
